title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): motives over a field k ⊂ C, treated tannakianly. The data a)–g) are as follows.
- G is a Q-group, thought of as Aut⊗ of the Betti fibre functor T_B.
- G' = Aut⊗(T_DR) is a k-group.
- P is a (G, G') bitorsor of isomorphisms T_B⊗k ≅ T_DR.
- There is a Hodge realization T_Hdg with group G'' and a bitorsor Q.
- i1, i2 : G_{m,C} → G''_C (equivalently into G_C) give the Hodge bigrading T^{ij}. In modern terms this is the Deligne torus h : S_C → G_C.
- φ is the comparison T_DR⊗_k C ≅ T_B⊗_Q C.

This page continues the list of necessary conditions on such data if they come from motives.

(1) Π(Spec k, ξ) → G. The marginal note 'groupe fondamental motivique' suggests Π is the motivic fundamental group (motivic Galois group) of Spec k at the fibre functor ξ, mapping to the group G of the realization data. Grothendieck asserts the following. The image of the identity component must lie in the smallest Q-rational subgroup of G whose complexification contains i1(G_m), i2(G_m). That subgroup is precisely the Mumford–Tate group, named as such on the next page. Under the Hodge conjecture, this is the expected statement G_mot° = MT.

(2) NB: Hodge symmetry (the second half of condition 1) singles out an element ψ ∈ Q(C). It is the comparison T_DR⊗C ≅ T_B⊗C for which complex conjugation exchanges T^{ij} and T^{ji}. This is a canonical complex point of the Hodge/de Rham torsor fixed by the reality condition on the bigrading.

(3) Re NB: if the data come from a category of motives over k, the Tate object yields a character G → G_m (resp. G' → G_m). Pushing out the torsor gives P ×^G G_m ≅ G_m ×^{G'} P, a G_m-torsor. On the de Rham side the Tate motive has a canonical k-rational generator, the marked point α, giving α_C ∈ (P ×^G G_m)(C). The comparison point φ̇ ∈ (P ×^G G_m)(C) induced by the period isomorphism then satisfies φ̇ = (1/2πi)·α_C. Hence 2πi·φ̇ is k-rational. This is an arithmetic (non-Hodge-theoretic) constraint on the data. It is the statement that the period of Q(1) is 2πi, phrased as a constraint on the complex point of the period torsor.

(4) Remarque: data a)–g) satisfying the Hodge-type conditions amount to tensor categories over Q mapping to the category of systems (V_Q, V_C = ⊔V^{ij}, V_k). Here V_k ⊂ V_C is a k-structure ('restriction of scalars from C to k') compatible with the natural Hodge filtration on V = V_Q⊗C. In modern terms this is the Tannakian category of Hodge structures with a k-rational de Rham structure, i.e. a Betti–de Rham–Hodge realization category. The motivic Galois group maps to its Tannaka group. The next page draws the consequence: for such an object coming from a motive over k, the Mumford–Tate group (its identity component) must be definable over k via V_k. For algebraically closed k, Hodge tensors must be k'-rational in de Rham, an absolute-Hodge type condition.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. Normalization of 2πi (φ̇ = α_C/2πi versus α_C = φ̇/2πi) depends on the convention for Q(1); the conclusion 'k-rational up to 2πi' is convention-independent.

The direction/meaning of Π(Spec k, ξ) → G is ambiguous on the page. If Π were the étale fundamental group, the natural map would go G → Gal, not Gal → G. The reading as the motivic fundamental group is more coherent with the marginal note.
'Sub-group generated by i1, i2' should be 'smallest Q-subgroup whose complexification contains the images', i.e. the Mumford–Tate group (implicitly what is meant).

ideas.what: Identity component of the motivic Galois group lands in (equals, under Hodge conjecture) the Q-subgroup generated by the Hodge cocharacters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (1966) for MT groups; Serre / Deligne (Deligne–Milne 1982) for the motivic statement
ideas.where_published: Expectation recorded via Saavedra Rivano (1972) and Deligne–Milne (1982); not in a Grothendieck publication to my knowledge

ideas.what: Canonical complex point ψ of the Hodge/de Rham torsor defined by Hodge symmetry conj(T^{ij}) = T^{ji}
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / Weil-type operator on the Hodge torsor

ideas.what: Period of the Tate motive as a point of the pushed-out G_m-torsor P ×^G G_m; constraint that 2πi·φ̇ is k-rational
ideas.modern_name: Period torsor; period of Q(1) = 2πi; ingredient of Grothendieck's period conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, via André, Lang footnote); Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, (2πi)^p normalizations); Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) on the transcendence of 2πi / periods, as reported by André; torsor formulation not published by him

ideas.what: Category of Hodge structures equipped with a k-structure V_k on V_C compatible with the Hodge filtration, as the target of motivic realizations
ideas.modern_name: Category of (Betti–de Rham–Hodge) realizations; Hodge structures with k-de Rham structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne ('Valeurs de fonctions L', 1979; 'Hodge cycles on abelian varieties', 1982); Jannsen (1990); Huber (1995)

missed.claim: A 1965 manuscript formulation of the realization category (V_Q, V_C = ⊔V^{ij}, V_k) with a k-structure compatible with the filtration. It is presented as the Tannakian target of the motivic fundamental group, together with the expectation G_mot° ⊂ MT. This predates Deligne's realization categories and Deligne–Milne by over a decade. Priority detail rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: structure de Hodge V(V_Q, V_C = ⊔V^{ij}, V_k), i.e. avec une variation sur k des V = V_Q ⊗_Q C = ⊔ V^{ij} avec sa filtration naturelle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that the Hodge–de Rham realization picture and the Mumford–Tate expectation for motivic Galois groups were already in Grothendieck's 1965 framework. Relevant for historical attribution.

missed.claim: Explicit torsor-theoretic formulation of the 2πi period constraint: the Tate character pushes P to a G_m-torsor with a k-rational de Rham point α, and the period point equals α_C/2πi. This is an early written instance of the period-torsor viewpoint behind the Grothendieck period conjecture.
missed.quote: on aura φ̇ = (1/2iπ) α_C ..., ce qui est une restriction arithmétique sur les données a) à g), savoir que 2iπ φ̇ est rat/k
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Primary-source evidence for the genesis of the period conjecture in torsor form (later made explicit by André and Kontsevich).

deep.surprise_reason: All ideas are now standard: MT = G_mot° under the Hodge conjecture, the period torsor and 2πi, and Hodge–de Rham realization categories. The page is a notably early (1965) manuscript instance of them in tannakian form, valuable for attribution but not containing unknown mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note under Π(Spec k, ξ) reads 'Groupe fond. motiviques' (likely 'groupe fondamental motivique').
'(à moins que on ne l'ignore[?])' is uncertain; it may be a sign/normalization caveat such as '(à un signe près ...)'.
Crossed word after i1, i2 line is probably 'assez' or 'aussi'; it is irrelevant.

In the Remarque, '{+variables[?]+}' is more likely 'variations' or 'structures' ('⊗-foncteurs compatibles aux structures'); later '{+variation[?]+} sur k' is likely 'restriction [des scalaires] à k', consistent with the next page.
